title: Security hardening: least-privilege IAM for fleet-provisioner + credential rotation
author: Gabe Wilson
description:
Context: As part of the Provision-to-ready automation sprint, the fleet-provisioner service is now the orchestration entrypoint for creating/expanding Dedicated pools (Terraform apply, bootstrap, and readiness gates). In its current form it inherited broad, admin-ish IAM permissions and long-lived credentials that are inappropriate for a high-churn automation path. This PR restricts fleet-provisioner to least privilege, scopes permissions by pool/environment, and rotates credentials to short-lived auth. It also adds an explicit security review checklist for future provisioning-related changes.

What changed (high level): (1) Replace the fleet-provisioner AWS creds path with IRSA (web identity) and remove static access keys from the service deployment. (2) Split the old shared role into two roles: fleet-provisioner-control (reads/writes provisioning state + emits events) and fleet-provisioner-terraform (assume-role into per-env, per-region apply roles). (3) Introduce a per-environment apply role with tight resource constraints (tags, prefixes, and explicit actions). (4) Add policy tests (policy simulation + unit tests over the generated policy JSON) and a “deny-by-default” safety net for actions outside approved regions/arns. (5) Rotate the remaining third-party credentials used for artifact mirror access and move them to sealed secrets with a rotation runbook step.

IAM changes (detail): - Removed: ec2:* (broad), iam:PassRole (unscoped), eks:* (broad), s3:* on all buckets, kms:* on all keys. - Added: a small set of specific EC2/EKS actions required by the Terraform modules plus read-only describe calls used by the orchestrator, all constrained by Resource + Condition (aws:ResourceTag/redwood-pool-id, aws:RequestTag/redwood-env, and aws:RequestedRegion). - PassRole is now limited to the exact node instance profile roles used by Dedicated pools (pattern: redwood-dedicated-node-*), and only from the terraform apply role. - KMS access is limited to encrypt/decrypt for specific key aliases used by provisioning outputs/state (alias/redwood/provisioning/*) with encryption context restrictions.

Operational behavior changes: - fleet-provisioner no longer starts if static AWS keys are present in its env; this is intentional to prevent backsliding. - If the orchestrator tries to apply outside the allowlisted regions, the run fails early with a clear error and an audit log entry. - Credential rotation is now part of the staging rollout checklist (doc updated).

Risk/rollout: - This is gated behind the existing staging flag for the new provisioning pipeline. - We tested staging applies in us-west-2 and eu-central-1. - Rollback path: re-enable the previous role binding in helm values and redeploy fleet-provisioner; no data migrations.

Security review checklist (added to /docs/security/provisioning-checklist.md): - Confirm service uses short-lived credentials (IRSA/workload identity) - Confirm IAM policies are least privilege with Resource/Condition constraints - Validate policy via IAM simulation (include output) - Ensure no secrets in helm values or CI logs; verify secret scanning passes - Confirm audit log events include actor/run_id/pool_id and are queryable - Ensure break-glass path (if any) is admin-only, time-bounded, and audited - Confirm runbook includes rotation and rollback steps

Testing: - Unit tests for policy generation and guardrails - Integration test: assume-role + plan/apply in staging with a minimal pool module - Manual: verified CloudTrail events include expected role session name and tags

Docs: Updated the provisioning runbook and security checklist; added notes to oncall about the new failure mode when a role is missing permissions.

Refs: ENG-2755 (RBAC/IAM tightening). INT-1044 (staging pipeline failure due to missing permission).
commits: infra/security: introduce per-env terraform apply roles with resource constraints
fleet-provisioner: switch AWS auth to IRSA and remove static key support
policy: add IAM simulation-based tests + generated policy snapshots
docs: add provisioning security checklist + update rotation/runbook steps
observability: add audit fields for role session name + env/pool tags
review_conversation: Marcus Lin (Security): Can you confirm there are zero static AWS keys referenced anywhere in helm values or CI? Also, please include the IAM simulation output for the “happy path” and one expected deny case.

Gabe Wilson (Author): Confirmed. I added a startup check that hard-fails if AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID is set, and I scrubbed the helm chart values. Added simulation outputs to tests/security/README and attached the deny case (attempt to create a security group without redwood-pool-id tag gets AccessDenied as expected).

Kevin Osei (Security): The kms permissions look too broad: kms:Decrypt on * with an alias condition is still risky if alias changes. Can we restrict to key ARN(s) for the provisioning keys in each env?

Gabe Wilson (Author): Good call. Updated env tf to output explicit key ARNs and wired the policy generator to use those ARNs; removed wildcard + alias-only constraint. Added an assertion test to prevent “*” resources in kms statements.
Rafael Mendes (SRE): What’s the failure mode during rollout if IRSA is misconfigured? We need a clear operator message and a quick rollback step.

Gabe Wilson (Author): Added a preflight that checks for the projected web identity token and prints a one-line actionable error pointing to the runbook section. Runbook now includes rollback steps (switch role binding back + redeploy).
Ethan Park (Control Plane): Any change to the API authz surface? Just making sure we didn’t inadvertently widen who can trigger a provisioning run.
Gabe Wilson (Author): No changes to API authz in this PR. This is strictly runtime identity and IAM permissions used by the service once it’s authorized to run.
Vanessa Ortiz (Fleet): Please make sure the per-region allowlist doesn’t block AP-southeast-1 when we bring up the next pilot pool.

Gabe Wilson (Author): Added ap-southeast-1 to the allowlist but kept it disabled by default in prod; it’s enabled in staging. Also documented how to extend the allowlist with a PR + security review checkbox.
Marcus Lin (Security): Looks good now. Approved contingent on CI green and the kms change landing (which it did).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Connor O'Brien. Post-merge note: staged rollout requires updating the service account annotation to the new role ARN; tracked in the staging checklist.
release_notes: Security: fleet-provisioner now uses short-lived credentials and least-privilege IAM roles; added provisioning security review checklist and updated runbooks for rotation/rollback.
